outcome: Understand public notices and signs, including timetables and advertisements.
Identify and select correct details from simple Urdu texts.
Select and organise relevant information from blogs, brochures, emails, forms, letters, magazines, newspapers and web pages.
Identify ideas, opinions and attitudes in a range of texts.
Understand implied meaning such as gist, opinion and the writer's purpose.
Identify important points or themes in an extended text.
Draw conclusions and recognise connections between ideas in a longer text.
Communicate facts, ideas and arguments in short and extended writing and translation in accurate Urdu.
Respond to a written stimulus in a suitable register and format, such as a summary, email, article, blog, report or review.
Use and manipulate a range of grammatical structures, punctuation and vocabulary.
Express opinions in suitable register and style.
Select and organise ideas into coherent paragraphs using linking devices.
Skim a short text and give single-word or phrase answers (Exercise 1).
Match sentences to the right short paragraph (Exercise 2).
Make brief notes under given headings from a longer text (Exercise 3).
Write a summary of no more than 100 words in your own words (Exercise 4).
Write a functional piece of about 150 words, such as an email, for a stated purpose and audience (Exercise 5).
Transform sentences with given prompts without changing meaning (Exercise 1).
Complete a multiple-choice cloze applying verb forms, agreement, comparatives, parts of speech and postpositions (Exercise 2).
Write about 200 words of continuous prose from prompts for a stated purpose and audience (Exercise 3).
Translate a passage of about 150 words from English into Urdu (Exercise 4).
